title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing Española after police stopped their car on July 23. A Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, reading the final digit as 7 instead of 2, and flagged the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers pulled over 21-year-old Jaclynn Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked an officer to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but the officer instead handcuffed the child.

The sisters filed lawsuits on January 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was wrongly stopped in April after being mistaken for an armed robbery suspect and forced to kneel with his hands on his head. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are now pending in state District Court.
